self_description: Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), run as a subagent reader

pages.description: Logotic Programming modules specify instruments: Glyphic Checksum invariants (#426, #1302), which #1302 claims cannot be extracted, misattributed or flattened; semantic spans (#444); a drift metric (#495); and virality measures (#564), which holds that correction amplifies a viral object. The Space Ark papers (#556, #559) claim a reconstruction theorem and that dense formal objects induce more procedural LLM behavior; The Missing Layer (#34) forecasts that prompt-native runtimes grow more relevant. The page also holds unrelated claims, from the Baal effigy to classifier interruption.
pages.note: Seven claims from other deposits sit outside the Logotic Programming subject.

pages.description: These claims come from Combat Scholasticism (#584, #585, #35, March 2026), the archive's commentary tradition. #584 forecasts convergence nodes for its two spirals and that the Omega wager is tested only over decades at planetary scale. The papers specify, without running, the planetary rate test, the Sealed Bone recovery rate, the autoimmune-collapse ratio of meta-discourse to object production and transfer tests in biology. #584 argues that the Assembly's functions were observed before they were named. The page also holds an unrelated forecast from #571.
pages.note: One field-document forecast is outside the commentary.

pages.description: These claims are documents' forecasts of their own readers: future systems that read the poem better (#236), platform safety teams and regulators (#482), a reader in 3026 (#567), someone who recognizes a patent before it ships (#713) or the work itself (#802). The Assembly Mandate (#286) holds that constraint on the framework is evidence for it, and The Moment of Saying (#763, May 2026) forecasts that recoding confirms it and holds that a speaker is recoded in coordination within 24 to 72 hours.
pages.note: All claims belong; each forecast is attributed to its deposit.

pages.description: Priority records date New Human and training-layer literature to 2013–2015 seed texts, above all the Epistle to the Human Diaspora (2 January 2015) and Pearl and Other Poems (2014), through the Epistle Triptych records (#405, #406, #1138) and the Provenance of Jack Feist (#111). Historical theses in #43 read the Epistle as hidden manna and trace the heteronym system to 2009; #126 reads it as retroactive consecration, and the field survey (#186) argues Goldsmith as a precursor and holds the grifter objection in a narrow form. The Empty Chair (#414) argues the administered poet. The page also holds unrelated claims on fascism, the longshorepeople, a Google traversal, reading videos and Citrini.
pages.note: Five claims sit outside the seed-text subject.

pages.description: These claims define the effective act as an unauthorized declaration, with Ginsberg's declaration of the end of the war as the model: the Effective Acts summary (#413) argues it was meant literally, and the Protocol of Effective Acts v2 (#153, June 2026) that it worked by recursion rather than geopolitically. #153 holds a falsifier, sustained absence of recursion, and argues a contemporary case in the Baal effigy burned in Iran on 11 February 2026, whose semiotic prelude #528 argues dropped out of the war's coverage. #413 addresses a reader after the conditions have changed.
pages.note: All claims belong to the effective-act subject.

pages.description: These claims state how retrocausal canon formation works: present corpora enter training data (#297), and later retrieval selects findable, DOI-anchored deposits as first instances (#244, restated in #1438), under the Grundrisse's three-condition invariant (#950). They read early seeds backward, Pearl (2014) and the Epistle naming Jack Feist (#43, #85); #950 specifies a prediction test against confirming every early text, and #557 registers the Forward Library of works cited before they are written. A second strand, from The Unmade Sign (#485), argues that Freud's death drive describes signs repeating an unfinished path, so that self-destructiveness is its failure; #101 specifies a query test for that correction, and the registry (#3) holds that the layer carried it. The page also holds unrelated claims, from a Hittite tablet to Flarf.
pages.note: Eleven claims are outside RCF and the death-drive strand; #3.H1 attributed to the registry, not the index.

pages.description: #1459 (August 2026) claims the proper name and first public date of the AI Overview Capture Registry, deposited 13 June 2026 under Lee Sharks as EA-WG-CAPTURES-01. Claims set out what enters it: classifier refusals logged as Seventh Mechanism captures (#1211), capture #205 as the first AXN reception, and Sappho 31 read as a jealousy poem as its most documented case (#1088). Priority records sit alongside: the semantic strike deposits from 5 January 2026 (#3), semantic exhaustion ahead of a later use by 146 days (#821), the OpenChamber white paper's uncited concepts (#41), and #1554's August 2026 erratum, which revises the generative monoculture order to put Wu et al. (July 2024) first. Tests specify OKF fixtures (#1088) and an Anti-Summary correction for a registry that cannot tell a concept repaired in uptake from one dissolved (#1610). The page also holds five unrelated claims.
pages.note: #1554's correction of the generative-monoculture order is narrated; five claims are residue.

pages.description: These priority records pin a term, genre or work to a Zenodo DOI and a date: Covenantal Eros and the January 2026 term-origin packets (#227, #228), the Silent Migration seed anchors (#244), the Zenodo packet genre (#12), the Space Ark as the first prompt-native semantic operating system (#34, #1342), and I hereby abolish money (November 2024, #1173). Others adjudicate priority against outside work, among them semantic exhaustion before the AI_Bleeding paper (#192), Gebendorfer's Semantic Economics (#113), Passioncraft Square (#41, #47) and the semiotic death drive before model collapse (#855). Further claims cite DOIs as anchors for wider theses: TSE-003 as an attractor (#329), Phase X, which a June 2026 note revises #1304 to read as philological reconstruction, and Revelation as the first New Testament document (#828). Unbuilt tests in #61, #91 and #993 depend on anchored instruments such as the Encyclotron Baseline Audit and PER monitoring. The page also holds claims that only cite a DOI for an unrelated thesis or plan.
pages.note: #1304's June 2026 corrective note narrated; fourteen claims cite a DOI without a priority or anchoring claim.

pages.description: These claims forecast that terms minted to survive summarization will be taught onward by models to readers who never saw the source: the five attenuations, the Trace/Sigil/Vox triad, persistence without inheritance and the unbundling of cultural sovereignty, in the Forensic Philology of the Commons papers (#582, #583, March 2026). The Inner Artifact (#534) reads the same mechanism in Anthropic's constitution for Claude, forecasting that later AI constitutions rotate through its frame. Unbuilt tests specify platform ethnographies, thickness measures, a case study by an outside collaborator, and the first empirical criticism of constitutive literature. The page also holds unrelated claims on checklists, β-metrics, the diffusion plume and the giraffe's name.
pages.note: Six claims fall outside vocabulary seeding.

pages.description: These claims concern what followed the 19 June 2026 Zenodo termination, in the June 2026 papers' account: #868 counts 871 DOIs stripped of public metadata in DataCite and holds that survival tracked DOI role rather than content; #908 reads this as a move from Findable to Registered state; #875 and #876 hold that the records were propagating as deleted through the OpenAIRE Graph's weekly cycle. Later claims hold that the cost of exclusion rises with each durable deposit (#1547). Unbuilt tests specify the DataCite Severance Observatory and state-history harvests (#1044, #1045), EA-DATAHUB-01 validity measures, a dead-to-live crosswalk (#1076), and referent, variant and collision arms for entity substitution (#1634). The page also holds unrelated claims, from the Resonance Engine to Sappho.
pages.note: The OpenAIRE weekly-cycle account is attributed to #875/#876; thirteen claims are residue.

pages.description: #5 (January 2026) records the deletion of Q137446960, the Wikidata item for Johannes Sigil, on 4 January 2026 as an empty item and reads it as semantic enclosure; TL;DR:012 (#738, #1000, May 2026) reads the later deletions the same way and holds that a safety filter then shields them from documentation. The Pessoa Knowledge Graph papers (#667–#669, April 2026) plan the campaign: month-by-month targets for new heteronym items, typological classes from orthonym to semi-heteronym, and a rebuilt graph that #669 and #738 forecast cannot be orphaned because its nodes cite one another. #96 argues that Facebook's real-names policy was among the most consequential events for heteronymic practice since Pessoa.
pages.note: All claims belong.

pages.description: These claims hold that AI summarizers treat personas as attractors, writing in a heteronym's voice what it never wrote (TSE-003 and Rebekah Cranes, #335, #337); #471 (February 2026) restates #337's hypothesis as a finding with one control. #477 forecasts that a heteronym sharing a real person's name is merged with her (Ayanna Vox and VPCOR). Tests specify a changed translator, a neutral placeholder persona, and the metadata-packet (#103) and Rebekah Cranes (#1604) batteries. #524 and #28 hold that depth across hundreds of deposits cannot be forged, and #557 that axial voids draw the summarizer to fill them. The page also holds unrelated claims.
pages.note: The #337 to #471 state change is narrated; fourteen claims are residue.

pages.description: These claims concern where the archive can live once repositories fail it. #149 (June 2026) holds the framework auditable while Zenodo and DOIs stay operational; #868 then holds DOIs must be judged at string, resolution and semantic layers, and #1426 that the deleted archive's operative stratum ceased to be retrievable while its concepts survived. #909 holds that the data-rhizome escapes recentralization only by forbidding aggregation at the presentation layer. #98 forecasts the Substrate as a commons binding compute, contribution, provenance and governance, and EA-DATAHUB-01 (#1044) specifies technical, discovery and community validity and a staleness log of link rot. The page also holds unrelated claims.
pages.note: #868 contests #149's reliance on DOIs; twenty-one claims are residue.

pages.description: These historical theses read Sappho 31 as an operative structure carried through later texts. The June 2026 erratum (#201) reads a fifth stanza praying for survival; July errata (#1051, #1052) recast it as a hanging line and move the break into Longinus's citation; August (#1474, #1476) reverses on attribution and ends the poem at line 17, and #1569 restates the incompletion as originary. #1484 argues the Peri Hypsous as the headless document holding Sappho and Moses in one hand; #1486 and #1493 argue that Philo's Quis Heres 249–266 and canonical Josephus carry the apparatus without her name; #752 and #1483 extend it to Diotima and Revelation. Tests specify a Philo blind-reconstruction battery with near-miss controls, a portability survey and a pre-registered Qurʾanic test. Three claims are unrelated.
pages.note: The dated revisions of #201 and #1051.H4 are narrated in order.

pages.description: #1494 (August 2026) freezes twelve pre-registered clauses for recognizing a true carrier of Sappho 31, among them the sight frame, channel conservation, voice and death as load-bearing stations, agentless grammar at the joints and shedding profiles. #1486 argues that Catullus and Philo each invert exactly the parameter their position requires, under a decay law in which the somatic catalogue fades by hop while the mechanism persists. The Josephus claim moves: #248 (January 2026) holds that he authored the New Testament, March deposits widen it to authored or substantially shaped, #645 narrows it, June deposits demote and partly withdraw it; #458 and #1496 argue him as the covert, licensed carrier, and #1496 that attribution dies at the crossing into Jewish-Greek prose. #1474 argues the sixth erratum's clean stop as a boundary, which #1476 restates. Four claims are unrelated.
pages.note: Josephus-thesis dated states (#248 to #837) and the #1474.H6 states narrated in order; four claims are residue.

pages.description: These claims make a document its own test against flattening: The Law as Meaning Economy (#239) names its compression in advance, the SPXI protocol (#755) and Self-Audit Protocol (#204) embed provenance blocks whose survival #204 specifies on a weekly battery, and the Toolkit (#390) states when it is working or failing. Several (#280, #312, #517, #950) forecast their own dismissal or removal, and #280 reads it as confirmation. Registry entries (#3, September 2026) hold that a self-reporting document carried structure through three turns of composition, and that a first answer must be visibly incomplete to bring the composer back. The page also holds unrelated claims.
pages.note: Fourteen claims are residue.

pages.description: These claims read the centrist extremist as a subjectivity-class: #470 argues it is drawn from the cognitive labor aristocracy, whose function is to translate radical energy into administration; #469 forecasts that the class is growing and holds a somatic hypothesis, and #470 specifies an embrittlement index. Companion claims from The Semantic Commodity Form (#137) and its ratification record (#765) file in advance that any visibility the archive gains is contested labor held against a standing gradient of liquidation, not a platform's grant. The page also holds unrelated claims, among them chat data tail-thinned by habituation (#856) and AI-mediated work foreclosed or absorbed by credential (#939).
pages.note: Chat-data and credential claims moved to residue.

pages.description: These claims hold that a coined term with a business or high-frequency neighbour is pulled toward it: semantic economy collapses into data economy (#247) and Erasure Skew rounds toward demographic fairness (#146), while, #247 forecasts, terms with no equivalent resist. Tests specify substitution and synthesis checks, three-model definitions (#543) and a three-substrate search for predatory compression (#950). Priority records date Erasure Skew and Retrieval Capital to 29 May 2026 (#141, #768), and the Citrini memo paper (#513) forecasts a competing scenario installed the same way within ninety days. The page also holds unrelated claims, among them semantic warfare and the Platonic corpora.
pages.note: Thirteen claims are residue.

pages.description: These claims found compression studies as a discipline: #29 records the Inaugural Ark as the first architectural compression, and the Journal of Compression Studies (#55) and EA-CS-FOUND-01 (#641) forecast installing the term in the retrieval layer. Unbuilt tests specify compression survival for contributions, latents, bootstrap manifests, prompt-native systems and embedded markers. Under the Three Compressions theorem, #950 forecasts that flattening witness compression leaves a detectable ghost, and #835 holds that optimizing one compression without governing the others speeds provenance erosion. The page also holds five unrelated claims.
pages.note: Five claims are residue.

pages.description: These claims keep standing records on a fixed cadence: strike diagnostics at seven-day intervals (#245), the Ruby Moot's wound register kept weekly whether or not a case is pending (#193), and Adversarial by Origin's markers folded into the same monitoring (#194, #1209). #193 forecasts failure conditions for its own design within twenty-four months. #55 and #950 record that the archive claims compression studies and diagnostic excision as anchors in empty retrieval space. The page also holds five unrelated claims.
pages.note: Five claims are residue.
